subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Find the centre, eccentricity, foci, length of the latus rectum and equations of the directrices of the hyperbola 4(y + 3)² − 9(x − 2)² = 1.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Senior Inter Maths-2B (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.100 — Star Questions Plus, answer 211, under the page's own 'HYPERBOLA' banner (the ONLY Hyperbola entry in Star Q+; the run is bounded by answer 210 Ellipse on the p.99 tail and answer 212 Definite Integrals-VSAQ opening p.101). Printed appearance: AP 19. Star Q+ pages carry no chapter-section star rating of their own (that lives on the SAQ/VSAQ chapter tables, pp.49/76), so this card is not assigned a stars value from a Star Q+ table. The 1+1+1+1 split mirrors 78.1/78.2's OURS split, following the book's own (i)-(v) style even though this page does not print numbered sub-labels. No error found in the book's printed working for answer 211 — every intermediate value (a²=1/9, b²=1/4, e=√13/3, foci (2, −3±√13/6), directrices y=−3±3/(2√13), latus rectum 4/9) was re-derived independently and matches. insider_note: The shift only ever moves the centre, foci and directrices — the eccentricity and the latus-rectum length depend purely on a² and b², so compute those two numbers first and they never need adjusting for (h, k).

steps.label: Write in standard form
steps.margin_note: No mark of its own — every result below reads a, b and the shifted centre off this line.
steps.memory_tip: Match (y+3)² with (y−k)² to read k = −3, and (x−2)² with (x−h)² to read h = 2.
lines: so the transverse axis is vertical.
steps.why: This is the same standard form as before, but shifted: replace x by (x − 2) and y by (y + 3) throughout, so the centre moves from the origin to (2, −3) and every other formula below uses these shifted coordinates.
common_mistakes: Reading the centre as (2, 3) or (−2, −3) — matching (y−k)² with (y+3)² gives k = −3, and (x−h)² with (x−2)² gives h = 2.
Dividing the whole equation by the wrong number, or not dividing at all, so the right side does not read 1.

steps.label: Eccentricity
steps.margin_note: First mark. The shift makes no difference to this formula.
steps.memory_tip: y-term positive ⇒ divide by b, not a — exactly as in the un-shifted vertical case.
steps.why: As in the un-shifted case, when the y-term is positive the eccentricity divides by b, not a — shifting the centre changes nothing about this formula.
common_mistakes: Dividing by a instead of b inside the calculation.
Arithmetic slip adding 1/9 + 1/4 — the common denominator is 36, giving 4/36 + 9/36 = 13/36.

steps.label: Foci
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Add the shift (h, k) to the un-shifted focus formula.
steps.memory_tip: Foci sit directly above and below the shifted centre (2, −3), not the origin.
steps.why: The foci sit on the transverse axis through the shifted centre (h, k) = (2, −3), at distance be above and below it, since the transverse axis is vertical here.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to add the shift (h, k) and writing the foci as if the centre were still the origin.
Placing the foci to the left/right of the centre instead of above/below — the transverse axis is vertical here.

steps.label: Equations of the directrices
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Horizontal lines through k ± b/e, shifted the same way as the foci.
steps.memory_tip: Directrices shift by the same (h, k) as the foci — same centre, same axis.
lines: Equations of the directrices: y = k ± b/e
steps.why: The directrices are horizontal lines through k ± b/e, shifted the same way as the foci.
common_mistakes: Writing the directrices as vertical lines — the transverse axis is vertical here, so the directrices are horizontal.
Dropping the −3 shift and giving only ±3/(2√13).

steps.label: Length of the latus rectum
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. The shift never affects this length.
steps.memory_tip: Latus rectum uses only a² and b² — never the centre — so this step is identical to the un-shifted case.
lines: Length of the latus rectum = 2a² / b
steps.why: The latus rectum length depends only on a² and b², never on the centre's shift.
common_mistakes: Using 2b²/a from the horizontal-axis formula instead of 2a²/b.
Second-guessing the result because of the shift, when the shift makes no difference here.
